# Rich Mentality — Module 02: Character Design Guide

**Status:** Reference art created (vector, 3D-style shading). **Not** a real 3D model and **not** generated by an image model. See "What this is" below.
**Research document `01_Economic_Research_and_World_Simulation.md` was read, not modified.**

---

## 1. What this is (and is not)

- The reference sheets are **vector illustrations drawn in code** (SVG → PNG) with soft gradient shading that imitates a simplified 3D-cartoon look. They fix the *design*: proportions, colours, face structure, clothing, expressions.
- They are **not** 3D renders. There is no mesh, rig or turntable. Skin, cloth and hair are shaded flat-ish.
- They **are** consistent by construction: every sheet comes from the same drawing code, so heights, colours and face structure cannot drift between images.
- Source SVGs are in `source_svg/` (editable in any vector editor); the generator is in `source_generator/`.
- To get true 3D-style renders, use the prompts in `External_3D_Generation_Prompts.md` with these sheets as the reference. Nothing here claims any external tool will reproduce them consistently — test first.

## 3. Shared style rules

- **Proportion:** head + hair ≈ 27% of height (about 3.6 heads tall). Deliberately stylised so faces read at 9:16 close-ups; bodies are simple tubes and blocks that are easy to rig.
- **Heights:** Emeka 100%, Sam 95%, Asha 88%. **Rule:** ground (sole bottom) to the highest point of the head silhouette, **including hair (Asha's curls, Sam's spikes) and Emeka's cap**; props are excluded. All sheets share one set of character units (Emeka = 1000, Sam = 950, Asha = 880). No sheet resizes a character on its own. Measured on the rendered images: see `Correction_Report.md`.
- **Shading:** one soft light from upper-left, darker right edge, soft contact shadow. Thin darker edge on clothing. No outlines on faces, no pores, no fabric texture.
- **Eyes:** large, glossy, white sclera, dark iris with two highlights. Brows carry most of the acting.
- **Rest pose:** A-pose, arms slightly out, neutral expression.
- **No logos, brands, luxury items or watches on anyone.**

## 4. Character identity guide

### Asha — 26, café cashier → baked-snack market stall (88%)

| Item | Spec |
|---|---|
| Face | Round, soft cheeks, small rounded chin |
| Eyes | Large round-ovals, strong upper lash line, medium-thick softly arched brows |
| Hair | Short dark curly hair as a cap of overlapping curls (#2A1D1A); curls fringe the forehead and wrap the temple and ear in the side view. **Silhouette = round puffy head** |
| Body | Soft and compact; boxy, slightly puffy jacket; shortest of the three |
| Clothing | Mustard jacket #E8A33D (ribbed hem, V-front, small collar, zip) · warm-cream inner shirt · trousers #3B4A5A · dark-brown practical shoes |
| Accessory | Small red notebook #C8493A, carried in hand |
| Story variation | Sage half-apron #6E9C94 tied over the jacket for the stall. Jacket stays visible so she remains recognisable |
| Signature | **Mustard jacket.** If only one thing survives in a shot, it is this |

### Emeka — 52, city bus driver (100%)

| Item | Spec |
|---|---|
| Face | Broad, squared jaw |
| Eyes | Medium round-ovals (smaller than Asha's, reads as mature); thick brows with grey streaks that sit just under the cap brim |
| Hair / beard | Grey tufts at the temples under the cap; full beard, charcoal base with grey (#8A8A8A) streaks and a moustache |
| Body | Tallest; broad square shoulders; solid, slightly heavy build |
| Clothing | Dark navy uniform #26405E (collar, two chest pockets, epaulettes) · black belt with plain buckle · slate trousers · black shoes · navy cap with a lighter-blue band |
| Accessory | Steel thermos #9AA5AD |
| Signature | **Cap + beard + wide shoulders** |
| Rules | No company logo anywhere. Never played as helpless or anti-ambition |

### Sam — 27, Asha's best friend and early partner (95%)

| Item | Spec |
|---|---|
| Face | Narrow, V-shaped chin |
| Eyes | Large almond-ovals, thin angular brows |
| Hair | Short, spiky, swept forward (#1E1E24); natural side section with a short sideburn and a hairline over the ear. **Silhouette = spikes** |
| Body | Tall and lean; angular shoulders; long thin legs |
| Clothing | Charcoal blazer #3A3F4B (notch lapels, two buttons) · light inner shirt · dark fitted trousers · white sneakers #F4F4F0 with white socks |
| Accessory | Smartphone with light-blue screen #7FD6E8 |
| Posture | Slight lean and head tilt; one hand in a pocket, phone in the other. No watch, no logos |
| Signature | **Spikes + blazer + white sneakers** |
| Rule | Not a villain. Polished, not rich |

## 5. Silhouette check

Head and hair separate the characters most strongly: Emeka = cap and very wide shoulders, Asha = round curly head and short stature, Sam = spikes and narrow frame. Below the neck, Asha and Sam are the closest pair (both mid-width torsos). They separate by **hem length, leg width, stance and height** rather than outline alone. If a shot is a pure silhouette, keep the heads visible.

## 6. Expression use notes

- **Asha:** ambition and vulnerability through brows and eyes; no melodrama. *Exhausted* and *Disappointed* are quiet.
- **Emeka:** warmth is the default. *Frustrated* and *Tired* should be about conditions (pay, staffing), never about ambition.
- **Sam:** *Envious* and *Competitive* are mild, deliberately subtle (side-glance, half-lid). He moves through them as a personal arc, not a statement about people in general.

## 7. The five improvements — how they were applied

| # | Requirement | How it shows up here |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Represent everyone, age-appropriate | Main cast is three adults, no children added just to fill the cast. Guidance for later: children = curious, patient, creative, building things; teens = skills, learning, planning. They must not act like adult investors or owners. Any future young character should reuse these style rules (same eye/brow language, simple shapes, no business props). |
| 2 | Geography | **No country is established, so none is implied.** No flags, currency, signage or landmark-specific clothing. Names and skin tones are *not* a location claim. Needs your decision (section 9). |
| 3 | Emeka realistic | Designed as a skilled, stable essential worker with an ordinary uniform. Nothing suggests he quits, or that buses vanish. Expressions cover strain (tired, concerned, frustrated) *and* pride and relief. |
| 4 | Sam personal | Polished but not rich: no luxury cues. Pressure is conveyed only by expression and posture, so it stays one person's story. |
| 5 | Unequal access | Different starting circumstances are hinted through objects, not stereotypes: Asha's analog notebook and everyday shoes, Emeka's thermos and uniform, Sam's smartphone. **This is a storytelling cue only**; it is not a claim that Asha has no phone or that any group lacks one. |

## 8. Changes I made from the brief

| Change | Reason |
|---|---|
| Stall apron is a **half-apron over the jacket** (not a full apron) | A full apron would hide the mustard jacket, her key identifier |
| Added colours the brief did not specify: cream shirt, shoe colours, Emeka's slate trousers, belt, cap band/epaulette blue `#3E6A98`, Sam's shirt, socks and soles, all skin tones, sage apron | Needed to complete the outfits. Each is tagged **"added by designer"** on the colour sheets |
| Emeka's beard = charcoal base + `#8A8A8A` streaks | "Grey-streaked" read literally; an all-grey beard looked flat |
| Sam's one-hand-in-pocket pose | Gives the distinct posture the brief asked for, and separates him from Asha in poses |
| Head ≈ 27% of height | Keeps faces expressive for vertical video. Larger than "slightly stylised" may imply (see section 9) |

## 9. Decisions that need your approval

1. **Production method.** The art is 2D with 3D-style shading. The project instructions allow 2D or 2.5D if it helps consistency. Do you want to (a) animate these directly as 2D/2.5D puppets, or (b) use them as references to build or generate true 3D?
2. **Setting and skin tones.** No location is established. I picked three distinct tones (Asha warm medium-brown `#B8754A`, Emeka deep brown `#6E4029`, Sam light warm tan `#D6A178`) for readable contrast. Please confirm them, or tell me the setting so they can be matched (and so nothing contradicts it).
3. **"Everyone" vs adults.** This brief says children and teenagers are included. The research document's assumption A1 and the earlier premise say adults only. I did **not** design child characters. Please confirm which rule governs before the story module.
4. **Head size.** Is 3.6 heads tall right, or should it be taller (more realistic) at the cost of smaller faces on vertical frames?
5. **Added colours** in section 8.

## 10. Known limitations

- Not 3D. No true volume; turnarounds are three separate drawings, not one model.
- Hands are simple mitten shapes with a thumb; they hold props but cannot gesture.
- Side and back heads are simpler than the front; fine for reference, not for close-ups. Side views face **left** for Asha and Emeka (props are in their left hands) and **right** for Sam (phone in his right hand).
- Expressions are drawn for the front view only.
- Asha's back-of-head curls are a stylised pattern.
- Not yet tested in any animation tool or external generator.

## 11. Final quality review

| Question | Result |
|---|---|
| Same animated world? | Yes: same shading, eye style, proportions and palette logic |
| Silhouettes distinct? | Mostly yes; strongest in the head and hair. Asha/Sam bodies are the closest pair (section 5) |
| Clothing recognisable? | Yes: mustard jacket, navy uniform + cap, charcoal blazer |
| Proportions consistent? | Yes: 100 / 95 / 88%, measured on every view and on the group and silhouette images (`Correction_Report.md`) |
| Reproducible across shots? | Yes, because they are generated from code; for an external tool, not yet tested |
| Expressions clear? | Yes at sheet size; Sam's *Envious* and Asha's *Disappointed* are the subtlest |
| Suitable for simple animation? | As 2D/2.5D puppets, yes. As 3D, needs modelling |
| Reflect the research and five improvements? | Yes (section 7), pending decisions 2 and 3 |
| Are actual images available? | **Yes: 12 PNGs** (3 model sheets + 1 variant, 3 expression sheets, 3 colour sheets, 2 group sheets). They are vector drawings, not generated 3D images |
